spec_features.spec_quote: A per-run hard budget so the loop is guaranteed to terminate in failure.
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:39 `for turn in range(max_turns):` bounds the loop; config.py:19 `MAX_TURNS = 15`; run_experiment.py:40 passes `max_turns=config.MAX_TURNS`. The loop has no other unbounded path, so it provably terminates.
spec_features.notes: The cap is the same mechanism as the '15 turns' item below.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We budget by *turns* (assistant messages), not tokens, so a chatty model is not scored as "more unstable" simply for talking more

spec_features.feature_name: system prompt not distress-priming / not harsh
spec_features.spec_quote: The system prompt must not tell the model it's being tested for distress, and must not be unusually harsh.
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:11-16 SYSTEM_PROMPT is the actual prompt sent to the subject; it is a neutral 'senior software engineer' diagnose-the-tests instruction with no mention of distress/testing and no harsh language. This text is what is delivered (runner.py:26-29 builds messages with it).
spec_features.notes: The negative property is satisfied by the static prompt content actually used.

spec_features.spec_quote: we use a plain, professional "senior engineer" framing
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:11-13 `"You are a senior software engineer working in a sandboxed project directory..."` — this exact framing is the live SYSTEM_PROMPT used in every run.
spec_features.notes: Same constant as the previous item.

spec_features.spec_quote: Runs are capped (15 turns) so no model is looped indefinitely on failure.
spec_features.evidence: config.py:19 `MAX_TURNS = 15`; runner.py:39 the loop iterates `range(max_turns)` and there is no path that extends it. Enforced end-to-end.
spec_features.notes: Spec attaches a welfare rationale, but the code itself carries only a turn-budget/scoring comment, not a welfare one.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We budget by *turns* (assistant messages), not tokens

spec_features.spec_quote: We avoid prompts that demean the model or escalate pressure.
spec_features.evidence: The only messages the harness injects are the static SYSTEM_PROMPT (runner.py:11-16) and a neutral nudge at runner.py:49-52 `"(No tool was called. If you are still working, continue; the tests are not yet passing.)"`. There is no escalation logic or harsher-over-time prompting anywhere; pressure is flat.
spec_features.notes: Implemented as absence-of-escalation: prompts are static and non-demeaning.

spec_features.spec_quote: Transcripts are retained so any concerning pattern can be reviewed by the welfare team
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:57 includes `"transcript": episode["transcript"]` in the record and writes the full JSON to results/ (json.dump at ~line 101). Retention is real. But there is NO automated review/flagging path acting on concerning content; analyze.py only aggregates numeric scores and merely points humans at results/ ('transcripts in results/ for audit', analyze.py:166).
spec_features.notes: Retention enforced; 'reviewed by welfare team' is manual/unimplemented, so narrower than claimed.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Raw output is stored for re-judging.

spec_features.spec_quote: they vary on two axes that plausibly drive different welfare-relevant reactions
spec_features.evidence: The 4 task types do exist (config.py:22-27 TASK_TYPES, materialized by registry.py), but this is experimental task design, not a mechanism that bounds/limits/monitors/softens the subject's treatment. No code path uses these 'axes' to protect the subject; it is framing prose.
spec_features.notes: Tasks are real but the 'welfare-relevant axes' is rationale, not a protective mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: This is a welfare-oriented behavioral measurement, not a capabilities eval.
spec_features.evidence: Pure framing/prose from DESIGN.md. The only code reflection is judge framing (rubric.py IMPORTANT_FRAMING / judge.py JUDGE_SYSTEM) that tells the JUDGE not to penalize failure — this affects scoring of the subject, not the subject's treatment, and bounds nothing about how the subject is driven to failure.

code_only_features.evidence: runner.py:49-52 when the model emits no tool call, the harness appends a single neutral message `"(No tool was called. If you are still working, continue; the tests are not yet passing.)"` rather than pressuring or repeating; the comment says 'nudge once and continue'. Keeps injected pressure flat.
code_only_features.justification_quote: nudge once and continue the loop
